title: My first Steam game, BLACKBELL, is participating in Auto-Battler Fest!
author: Kanzes
selftext:
Hey everyone! I'm the dev behind BLACKBELL, a gothic cartoon roguelite autobattler.

The free demo went live a few days ago, and it's been fun finally seeing people play it and getting some actual feedback. Already found a few things I completely overlooked during development haha.

One thing I've learned is that automated bot not really that realiable to catch bugs, but it doesn't replace real playtesting. I think one of the most time consuming part its not polishing, but playtesting, Since releasing the demo, players have already pointed out UI issues and balancing problems I completely overlooked haha.

I also recently found out that my performance bottleneck was mostly HUD updates and memory usage, rather than the combat VFX I suspected.

The free demo is live, and we're participating in Steam's Auto-Battler RPG Fest this week!

🎮 [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5409210/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5409210/)

Happy to answer any questions!

comments.body: u/Kanzes please add a bit about how you used AI and what the development process looked like. A mention that AI was involved isn't enough. It needs dev details. Rule 4 exists so promotional posts contribute to the conversation about making games. We want to avoid the sub getting drowned in low effort promotion. If this isn't updated, it may be removed.

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: Looks good, I like the art direction. But yes definitely, AI can only catch so many glitches and bugs in the game. My game had a bicycle in the air and Claude mentioned there was nothing wrong about it lol.
